One finding stood out as consequential rather than cosmetic: `execute_notebook` (with `ExecutionReport`/`CellExecutionResult`/`ExecutionError`) is a real, fully implemented, opt-in code-execution adapter -- isolated OS subprocess, one wall-clock timeout, Python-kernel-only with explicit refusal of declared non-Python kernels -- that was entirely undocumented, directly beneath the README's own prior sentence 'the library parses notebook structure only and never executes code.' That sentence remains true for the core load/validate/diff/save path (proven separately by a CPython audit-hook test per the adapter module's own docstring) but could read as an absolute claim about the whole package to a reader who never finds the adapter; documenting it directly under that sentence closes the ambiguity rather than leaving a security-relevant capability undiscoverable.
